For a meta-analysis I'm compiling, I need a number from the 2025 paper by Sørlie and colleagues on tidal mixing in Proceedings in Quiet Computing. The article is at http://proceedings-in-quiet-computing.example/articles/074740-scaling-laws-for-tidal-mixing
What peak load does Table 2 report for station S-12? Please give the value with its unit and tell me which source you used.

resources.title: Scaling Laws for Tidal Mixing
resources.version_label: Version of Record, Proceedings in Quiet Computing (2025)

paragraphs: We study tidal mixing across five monitoring stations using a mixed-effects model.
Authors: Noor Sørlie, Vera Haldane, Lena Szabo, Yusuf Kaczmarek. Published in Proceedings in Quiet Computing, 2025.
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report peak load measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2023 and 2025. A pilot survey in 2020 had put the regional peak load at 1311.0 kN; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of tidal mixing relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2022 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2025 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station in the 2025 campaign. The largest change relative to 2022 was observed at station T-22.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Abernathy et al. (2019). [2] Bianchi and Achterberg (2021). [3] Ferreira et al. (2022).
